title: Contributor Guide
content:
#

For contributors who help develop and maintain @antv/layout. This section
focuses on:

 * Contribution flow: clone, develop, test, and open PRs
 * Project structure: repository layout and key modules
 * Implementation overview: data model, execution pipeline, and Worker mechanism

Navigation:

 * workflow: contribution flow and common commands
 * structure: project architecture and key directories
 * internals: implementation overview (from BaseLayout to Worker)

title: Internal Implementation Overview
content:
#

This section walks through the implementation of @antv/layout from entry to
result.


1. Unified entry point: BaseLayout.execute#

All layout classes are built on BaseLayout (src/algorithm/base-layout.ts):

 * Merge default options with user options (mergeOptions)
 * Build the runtime context: RuntimeContext(data, { node, edge })
 * Decide whether to enable Worker: enableWorker && typeof Worker !==
   'undefined'
   * Enabled: use layoutInWorker
   * Disabled: call layout() on the main thread


2. Graph data model: RuntimeContext + GraphLib#

RuntimeContext wraps the input GraphData into a readable/writable graph object:

 * Uses GraphLib internally to store nodes/edges in Maps
 * Exposes helpers like forEachNode/forEachEdge
 * forEachEdge fills in sourceNode/targetNode to reduce repeated lookups

GraphLib handles two kinds of work:

 * Data structures: organize nodes/edges into Maps and keep _original references
 * Performance caches: build and cache degree, adjacency lists, index maps, and
   more on demand


3. Worker execution: Supervisor ↔ worker.ts#

Workers move computation off the main thread to avoid blocking.

 * Supervisor (main thread):
   * Resolve the worker script path (compatible with ESM/UMD)
   * new Worker(workerPath, { type }) and use Comlink wrap to create workerApi
   * Call workerApi.execute(layoutId, data, options) to get the result graph
 * worker.ts (worker thread):
   * Fetch the layout constructor from registry[layoutId] and run it
   * Force enableWorker = false to avoid spawning workers inside workers
   * Return layoutInstance.model.data() (final Maps of nodes/edges)

If a worker fails, it automatically falls back to the main thread (see the
try/catch in BaseLayout.layoutInWorker).


4. Iterative layouts: BaseSimulation pattern#

Some layouts converge iteratively (e.g., force-directed). BaseSimulation
provides shared control:

 * tick(n): run n iterations and trigger the tick callback
 * restart(): support animated and non-animated runs
 * stop(): stop the iteration loop

Each algorithm only needs to implement runOneStep(), returning the step's
movement or convergence metric.

title: Project Structure
content:
#


Directory overview#

 * src: core library source (algorithms, types, Worker entry, etc.)
 * lib: ESM build output (published)
 * dist: UMD build output (published)
 * site: docs site (Rspress)
 * __tests__: unit tests
 * perf: performance benchmarks and comparisons (optional)


Directory notes#

src contains the core implementation. Start with src/index.ts and
src/algorithm/base-layout.ts.

 * src/index.ts: public exports
 * src/registry.ts: layout registry (layoutId -> LayoutCtor)
 * src/algorithm/: layout implementations
   * base-layout.ts: base layout (unified entry, Worker support)
   * base-simulation.ts: shared logic for iterative/simulation layouts
     (tick/restart/stop)
 * src/model/: graph data model
 * src/runtime/: runtime capabilities
   * context.ts: RuntimeContext (wraps input data into an iterable graph
     context)
   * supervisor.ts: Worker management (init, invoke, teardown, path resolution)
 * src/worker.ts: Worker entry (Comlink expose)
 * src/types/: shared type definitions
 * src/util/: utilities


What to change when adding a layout#

Typically:

 1. Add an implementation in src/algorithm/ (extend BaseLayout, implement id +
    layout())
 2. Export it in src/algorithm/index.ts and src/index.ts
 3. Register the id in src/registry.ts
 4. Add tests in __tests__
 5. Add docs in site/docs/zh/guide/api/

title: Contribution Workflow
content:
#


Prerequisites#

 * Node.js >= 18.12
 * npm >= 9 (or a version matching the lockfile)


Install dependencies#




Local development#

Common workflows grouped by target:

 * Core layout library (repo root)
   * Start dev server: npm run dev
   * Build: npm run build
   * Test: npm test
 * Docs site (site)
   * Start: npm --prefix site run dev
   * Build: npm --prefix site run build
 * Full checks (recommended before a PR)
   * Build: npm run build
   * Test: npm test


Pre-submit checklist#

 * Keep changes minimal and focused (one PR, one purpose)
 * Add tests when behavior changes (__tests__)
 * Keep docs/examples consistent with code (update when adding layouts/params)


Versions and change logs (optional)#

This repo uses Changesets for release notes (.changeset/). To add a changeset:



New or updated changesets are aggregated into the changelog on release.


Open a PR#



Commit messages should follow the Angular convention (see CONTRIBUTING.md in the
repo root).

title: ComboCombined Composite Combo Layout
content:
#

Designed for composite scenes with combos or subgraphs. You can assign different
layout strategies per hierarchy level, while handling combo bounds and spacing
consistently.


When to use#

 * Composite structures with combos/groups/subgraphs
 * Different layout strategies by level, e.g. force on the outer layer and grid
   inside


Input requirements#

Composite layouts need clear hierarchy and combo nodes:

 * Normal nodes reference their parent combo via parentId
 * Combo nodes must have isCombo: true and an id

If your business fields differ, adapt them via the node mapping function. See
the data mapping section for details.


Usage#




Options#


Common options#

These options apply to all layouts and define the reference size, center, worker
usage, and field mappings.

OPTION           DESCRIPTION                                                    TYPE                                                    DEFAULT
width / height   Reference size. Many layouts derive default centers/scales.    number                                                  undefined
center           Layout center. 2D uses [x, y], 3D uses [x, y, z].              [number, number] | [number, number, number]             undefined (layout-dependent)
enableWorker     Run in a Web Worker when available; fallback to main thread.   boolean                                                 false/undefined (layout-dependent)
node             Node field mapping for business data.                          (datum) => ({ id?, x?, y?, z?, parentId?, isCombo? })   undefined
edge             Edge field mapping for business data.                          (datum) => ({ id?, source?, target? })                  undefined

Node mapping fields#

 * id: unique node id, required.
 * x/y/z: optional initial coordinates for warm start or continuous layouts.
 * parentId: parent combo id for composite or nested layouts.
 * isCombo: whether this is a combo node.

Edge mapping fields#

 * source / target: endpoint node ids, required. Must match some node id.

 * id: optional edge id. Auto-generated if omitted.


Algorithm options#

OPTION         DESCRIPTION                                          TYPE                                              DEFAULT
layout         Layout config. Can be fixed or chosen per comboId.   string | { type: string; ... } | (comboId)=>...   undefined
nodeSize       Node size                                            Size | (node)=>Size                               undefined
nodeSpacing    Spacing between nodes                                number | (node)=>number                           undefined
comboSpacing   Spacing between combos                               number | (combo)=>number                          undefined
comboPadding   Inner padding for each combo                         number | (combo)=>number                          undefined

Data requirements

If your source data lacks parentId/isCombo, add hierarchy information in your
business data or generate it in the mapping step.

title: D3Force3D (3D force)
content:
#

D3Force3DLayout is based on d3-force-3d, adding z-axis forces on top of 2D. It
is suitable for 3D scenes or depth-layered views.




When to use#

 * 3D rendering or layouts that need z coordinates
 * Reduce occlusion through depth layering


Input requirements#

 * Nodes must have unique id
 * edges are recommended because link forces depend on relationships


Usage#




Options#

This page lists all options for D3ForceLayout. It supports two configuration
styles:

 1. Shorthand fields: quick access to common settings like centerX,
    linkDistance, nodeStrength.
 2. Force objects: closer to the original d3-force API, such as link, manyBody,
    collide, x, y, center, radial.

You can mix both; when both are provided, the force objects are usually more
predictable.


Common options#

OPTION           DESCRIPTION                      TYPE                                                    DEFAULT
width / height   Reference size                   number                                                  undefined
enableWorker     Whether to run in a Web Worker   boolean                                                 false/undefined
node             Node field mapping               (datum) => ({ id?, x?, y?, z?, parentId?, isCombo? })   undefined
edge             Edge field mapping               (datum) => ({ id?, source?, target? })                  undefined

Note: D3ForceLayout does not use center; it uses centerX/centerY instead.


Shorthand fields#

OPTION                      DESCRIPTION                                           TYPE                             DEFAULT
onTick                      Tick callback                                         (layout) => void                 undefined
centerX / centerY           Center coordinates                                    number                           width/2, height/2
centerStrength              Center force strength in [0, 1]                       number                           undefined
edgeId                      Edge id accessor                                      (edge) => string                 (edge) => String(edge.id)
linkDistance                Ideal link length                                     number | (edge)=>number          50
edgeStrength                Link strength in [0, 1]                               number | (edge)=>number | null   null
edgeIterations              Link force iterations                                 number                           1
nodeStrength                Many-body strength; negative = repulsion              number | (node)=>number          -30
theta                       Barnes–Hut parameter in (0, 1]                        number                           undefined
distanceMax / distanceMin   Many-body distance range                              number                           undefined
preventOverlap              Prevent overlaps                                      boolean                          false
collideStrength             Collision strength in [0, 1]                          number                           1
collideIterations           Collision iterations                                  number                           1
nodeSize                    Node diameter used for collision radius               number | (node)=>number          10
nodeSpacing                 Extra spacing between nodes                           number | (node)=>number          0
radialRadius                Ideal radial radius                                   number                           100
radialStrength              Radial force strength in [0, 1]                       number                           undefined
radialX / radialY           Radial force center                                   number                           undefined
clustering                  Enable clustering                                     boolean                          false
clusterBy                   Cluster field/function                                (node)=>string|number            (d)=>d.cluster
clusterNodeStrength         In-cluster node strength                              number                           -1
clusterEdgeStrength         Inter-cluster edge strength                           number                           0.1
clusterEdgeDistance         Inter-cluster edge distance                           number                           100
clusterNodeSize             Cluster node size                                     number                           10
clusterFociStrength         Cluster focus strength in [0, 1]                      number                           0.8
iterations                  Force iterations; not the same as layout iterations   number                           undefined
forceSimulation             Custom d3 Simulation                                  Simulation                       undefined
alpha / alphaMin            Current/stop thresholds                               number                           undefined
alphaDecay                  Decay rate of alpha                                   number                           undefined
alphaTarget                 Target alpha                                          number                           undefined
velocityDecay               Velocity decay factor                                 number                           undefined
randomSource                Random generator                                      () => number                     undefined


Force objects#

These force objects can be set to false to disable; otherwise configure fields
as in d3-force.

collide#

 * radius?: number | (node, index, nodes) => number
 * strength?: number
 * iterations?: number

manyBody#

 * strength?: number | (node, index, nodes) => number
 * theta?: number
 * distanceMin?: number
 * distanceMax?: number

link#

 * id?: (edge, index, edges) => string
 * distance?: number | (edge, index, edges) => number
 * strength?: number | (edge, index, edges) => number
 * iterations?: number

x / y#

 * strength?: number | (node, index, nodes) => number
 * x?: number | (node, index, nodes) => number (only for x force)
 * y?: number | (node, index, nodes) => number (only for y force)


2D extensions#

OPTION   DESCRIPTION    TYPE
center   Center force   false | { x?, y?, strength? }
radial   Radial force   false | { radius?, x?, y?, strength? }


3D extensions#

D3Force3DLayout adds z-axis forces on top of 2D. Node results include z and may
keep intermediate velocities like vz.

OPTION          DESCRIPTION                    TYPE                                         DEFAULT
numDimensions   Dimensions, fixed at 3.        3                                            3
center          Center force with z support.   false | { x?, y?, z?, strength? }            -
radial          Radial force with z support.   false | { radius?, x?, y?, z?, strength? }   -
z               Z-axis force                   false | { z?, strength? }                    -

want to reuse the d3 force configuration style, combining link, manyBody,

title: ForceAtlas2 Layout
content:
#

ForceAtlas2 is designed for graph visualization, especially large graphs with
community/cluster structures, and offers acceleration options like Barnes–Hut.


When to use#

 * Force-directed layout for larger graphs
 * Emphasizing community/cluster structure


Input requirements#

 * Nodes must have unique id
 * edges are recommended since community structure depends on relationships


Usage#




Options#


Common options#

These options apply to all layouts and define the reference size, center, worker
usage, and field mappings.

OPTION           DESCRIPTION                                                    TYPE                                                    DEFAULT
width / height   Reference size. Many layouts derive default centers/scales.    number                                                  undefined
center           Layout center. 2D uses [x, y], 3D uses [x, y, z].              [number, number] | [number, number, number]             undefined (layout-dependent)
enableWorker     Run in a Web Worker when available; fallback to main thread.   boolean                                                 false/undefined (layout-dependent)
node             Node field mapping for business data.                          (datum) => ({ id?, x?, y?, z?, parentId?, isCombo? })   undefined
edge             Edge field mapping for business data.                          (datum) => ({ id?, source?, target? })                  undefined

Node mapping fields#

 * id: unique node id, required.
 * x/y/z: optional initial coordinates for warm start or continuous layouts.
 * parentId: parent combo id for composite or nested layouts.
 * isCombo: whether this is a combo node.

Edge mapping fields#

 * source / target: endpoint node ids, required. Must match some node id.

 * id: optional edge id. Auto-generated if omitted.


Iteration control#

These options control convergence for ForceLayout, ForceAtlas2Layout, and
FruchtermanLayout.

Execution modes#

 * execute(data): run in one go; frame-splitting is controlled by animate.
 * You can also wire layouts into your render loop via restart(), tick(n),
   stop(). See "Iterative layouts" in Common API.


Iteration options#

OPTION                  DESCRIPTION                                                    TYPE                     DEFAULT
maxIteration            Maximum iterations                                             number                   0/500 (layout-dependent)
minMovement             Convergence threshold. Stops when step size falls below this   number                   0/0.4 (layout-dependent)
                        value.
animate                 Run iterations in frames for visualization and interaction.    boolean                  true
dimensions              Dimensions: 2D or 3D.                                          2 | 3                    2
distanceThresholdMode   How to evaluate minMovement: mean, max, or min.                'mean' | 'max' | 'min'   'mean'
maxDistance             Maximum interaction distance; used by some algorithms.         number                   undefined
onTick                  Callback after each iteration; receives the layout instance.   (layout) => void         undefined


Algorithm options#

OPTION           DESCRIPTION                                              TYPE                        DEFAULT
kr               Repulsion coefficient. Higher = more spread.             number                      5
kg               Gravity coefficient. Higher = tighter center.            number                      1
ks               Speed coefficient                                        number                      0.1
ksmax            Maximum speed                                            number                      10
tao              Oscillation tolerance for convergence                    number                      0.1
mode             Mode. linlog emphasizes clusters.                        'normal' | 'linlog'         'normal'
preventOverlap   Prevent overlaps. Requires nodeSize.                     boolean                     false
nodeSize         Node size for collision detection.                       Size | (node) => Size       undefined
nodeSpacing      Spacing between nodes                                    number | (node) => number   undefined
dissuadeHubs     Hub mode; pulls high-degree nodes closer to center.      boolean                     false
barnesHut        Barnes–Hut acceleration; recommended for large graphs.   boolean                     undefined
prune            Auto-pruning for speed; may reduce quality.              boolean                     undefined

Performance tips

For large graphs, consider barnesHut: true. If speed matters most, try prune:
true, but it can affect quality.

title: Force Layout
content:
#

Force layout offers a highly configurable force-directed model, including link
distance, repulsion/attraction, centripetal force, and clustering. It is ideal
when you need fine-grained tuning and process control.


When to use#

 * Fine-grained control over force behavior
 * Engineering features like clustering, centripetal force, and monitoring
   callbacks


Input requirements#

 * Nodes must have unique id
 * edges are recommended since forces rely on relationships. It can run without
   edges, but results look like scattered points.


Usage#




Options#


Common options#

These options apply to all layouts and define the reference size, center, worker
usage, and field mappings.

OPTION           DESCRIPTION                                                    TYPE                                                    DEFAULT
width / height   Reference size. Many layouts derive default centers/scales.    number                                                  undefined
center           Layout center. 2D uses [x, y], 3D uses [x, y, z].              [number, number] | [number, number, number]             undefined (layout-dependent)

edge             Edge field mapping for business data.                          (datum) => ({ id?, source?, target? })                  undefined

Node mapping fields#

 * id: unique node id, required.
 * x/y/z: optional initial coordinates for warm start or continuous layouts.
 * parentId: parent combo id for composite or nested layouts.
 * isCombo: whether this is a combo node.

Edge mapping fields#

 * source / target: endpoint node ids, required. Must match some node id.

 * id: optional edge id. Auto-generated if omitted.


Iteration control#

These options control convergence for ForceLayout, ForceAtlas2Layout, and
FruchtermanLayout.

Execution modes#

 * execute(data): run in one go; frame-splitting is controlled by animate.
 * You can also wire layouts into your render loop via restart(), tick(n),
   stop(). See "Iterative layouts" in Common API.


Iteration options#

OPTION                  DESCRIPTION                                                    TYPE                     DEFAULT

minMovement             Convergence threshold. Stops when step size falls below this   number                   0/0.4 (layout-dependent)
                        value.

Algorithm options#

Force has a large option set; the table below lists all fields:

nodeStrength          Node force. Positive = attraction, negative = repulsion.   number | (node)=>number                   1000

title: Fruchterman Layout
content:
#

Fruchterman-Reingold is a classic force-directed layout. It uses repulsion,
attraction, and gravity to reach a balanced distribution on the plane.


When to use#

 * General force layout for small/medium graphs
 * Need a balanced global structure


Input requirements#

 * edges are recommended for attraction and structural constraints

title: Introduction
content:
#

@antv/layout is a layout algorithm library for graph visualization. It ships
with a wide range of layouts, unifies graph data and layout APIs, and turns
graph structures into renderable coordinates.


Layouts at a glance#

Force (iterative)   ForceAtlas2Large graphs with acceleration support.             ForceRich parameters and fine-grained control.
                    FruchtermanClassic force layout for small/medium graphs.       D3ForceA wrapper around d3-force simulation.
                    D3Force3D3D force layout with z output.                        
Hierarchy/flow      DagreDirected hierarchical layout with labels/placeholders.    AntVDagreProduction-grade Dagre variant.
Circular/radial     CircularCircular/spiral distribution with ordering controls.   ConcentricLayer by concentric value.
                    RadialRadial structure centered on a focus node.               
Regular/init        GridStable grid positions.                                     RandomRandom coordinates for placeholders.

title: Data Mapping
content:
#

This section explains how to adapt your business data to the layout input
format.

NOTE

If you already use the standard graph format where nodes use id and edges use
source / target, you can skip this section.


Why data mapping?#

Layouts depend on key fields like node id, edge source/target, and optional
initial coordinates. Business data often uses different field names. Mapping
lets you adapt fields without mutating the original data.


Example business data#

Assume your data looks like this:



WARNING

Running a layout directly on this data will fail because the fields are nodeId,
from, and to, not the expected id, source, and target.


Configure field mappings#

Pass node / edge mapping functions either at initialization or execution time.

Map only the required fields

Mapping functions only need to return fields required by the layout, such as id,
source, target, x, y. Other business fields do not need to be copied. The layout
result keeps _original pointing to the original object for easy read/write.


Node mapping#



The mapping function receives a raw node object and returns the fields needed
for layout:

Field reference:

FIELD                REQUIRED   NOTES
id                   ✅          Unique node identifier
x / y                           Optional initial position for warm start
z                               Optional 3D initial position for 3D warm start
parentId / isCombo              Hierarchy info for combo layouts such as Dagre, AntV-Dagre,
                                ComboCombined


Edge mapping#



Field reference:

FIELD    REQUIRED   NOTES
id                  Unique edge identifier
source   ✅          Source node id, must match some node id
target   ✅          Target node id, must match some node id

Edge id is optional

If id is omitted, it will be generated from source-target. For parallel edges, a
suffix is added, e.g. a-b-1.


Common extension: read business fields in callbacks#

Many layout options accept callbacks, such as nodeSize(node) and
linkDistance(edge). These callbacks usually receive the original business
object, so you can store custom fields and read them in the callback:




Full example#

This example shows the complete mapping flow:



The layout does not mutate the original data. Mapping is only used during
computation, and the results are exposed through the layout result objects.


Next steps#

After mapping your data, you can:

 * Explore layout algorithms
 * Entry point: Common API
 * Common options and compositions: Layout Configuration

Mapping lets you keep your business data intact while using the unified layout
input interface.

For pages without a build tool, use the UMD build. It exposes a global Layout.

Pin a version in production to avoid the uncertainty of latest.




Minimal example#




Worker notes#

When enableWorker: true is set and the environment supports Worker, layouts run
in a worker to reduce main-thread blocking.

In the UMD build, the worker script URL is derived from the current
index.js/index.min.js URL, pointing to worker.js in the same directory. Make
sure:

 * dist/worker.js is accessible and lives alongside dist/index.min.js.
 * Your site CSP and CORS settings allow loading the worker script.

If the worker fails to load, the layout automatically falls back to the main
thread.

title: Layout Configuration
content:
#

This page focuses on how to organize options, including common fields, typical
combinations, and practical guidance for choosing layouts. Topics include
size/center, node size, overlap prevention, workers, and warm start.


First, how options are merged#

Each layout constructor takes initialOptions, and execute(data, userOptions?)
accepts userOptions. They are merged at execution time:

 * Strategy: shallow merge, later fields override earlier ones
 * Priority: userOptions > initialOptions > layout defaults

This means:

 * Put long-lived parameters in the constructor, such as width/height and
   enableWorker.
 * Put per-run parameters in execute, such as center and nodeSpacing.


Common options: BaseLayoutOptions#

All layouts share fields from BaseLayoutOptions:

 * width / height: reference size for layout. Many layouts derive default
   centers or scales from it.
 * center: layout center ([x, y] in 2D, [x, y, z] in 3D).
 * enableWorker: whether to attempt running in a Web Worker; falls back to the
   main thread if unavailable.
 * node / edge: field mappings to adapt business data to
   id/source/target/x/y/....

For mapping details and examples, see Data Mapping.


Reading results: forEachNode / forEachEdge#

execute() does not mutate your input data; results are read via traversal:



Edge output fields depend on the layout:

 * Force-directed layouts typically only need source/target to apply forces
 * Dagre/AntV-Dagre may output edge.points, edge.labelPos, etc. for polylines
   and label routing


Workers: when and how#


When to enable#

 * Large graphs and iterative layouts, such as Force, ForceAtlas2, Fruchterman,
   D3Force
 * UI threads that need to stay responsive for dragging, zooming, or animations


How to enable#



Notes:

 * Only works in browsers with Worker support; otherwise it falls back to the
   main thread.
 * Bundlers must be able to load the library’s worker entry. Worker handling
   differs across frameworks, so verify in your target environment.
 * For UMD via CDN, the worker URL is derived from the script URL as worker.js
   in the same directory. See Installation.


Warm start (reuse existing coordinates)#

Many layouts use initial coordinates to warm-start and converge faster. You can:

 * Provide x/y directly in the data (standard fields)
 * Or map business coordinates to x/y via node




Node size and overlap prevention#

Many layouts rely on node size for collision/overlap detection:

 * Provide size on your business nodes (consumed via _original)
 * Or set nodeSize in options (number/size or callback)

Common pitfall:

 * Setting preventOverlap: true without size/nodeSize means collisions cannot be
   computed accurately


Choosing a layout: a practical starting point#

 * Dagre / AntV-Dagre: flowcharts, DAGs, hierarchies (needs edge direction,
   layer spacing, etc.)
 * Force / ForceAtlas2 / Fruchterman / D3Force: general relationship graphs
   (iterative, animatable)
 * Circular / Concentric: grouped or ordered circular views
 * Grid / Random: initial placement, placeholders, preprocessing
 * MDS: high-dimensional similarity projection (distance matrix or
   similarity-driven)
 * Radial: hierarchical/relational views centered on a focus node
 * ComboCombined: composite layout for combos/subgraphs (layout selection by
   hierarchy)

For detailed options, see Common API and each layout page such as Circular,
Force, and Dagre.

title: Using WebWorker
content:
#

When enableWorker: true and Worker is available, layout computation runs in a
WebWorker to reduce main-thread blocking.

However, if you pass function callbacks in options (e.g. (node) => ...), Worker
mode may throw errors like:




Why it happens#

The library transfers data/options between the main thread and the Worker via
structured clone. Functions are not structured-cloneable, so any function inside
options can break the transfer.


How to fix#


Option 1: Use Expr (string expressions) instead of callbacks#

@antv/layout supports Expr (powered by @antv/expr) for many numeric/size fields.
If a field’s type includes Expr, you can pass a string expression instead of a
function.

Example (ForceLayout):



Expression variable names depend on the field:

 * Node fields usually use node
 * Edge fields usually use edge
 * Combo fields usually use combo


Option 2: Pre-compute values into your data#

If you used to do:



You can pre-fill data.nodes[i].data.size and then use nodeSize: 'node.data.size'
(or rely on defaults).


Option 3: If you need callbacks, don’t enable Worker#

Some capabilities inherently require functions and cannot be passed into
Workers:

 * onTick-style callbacks
 * node / edge mapping functions
 * Any custom logic without an Expr alternative

In these cases, run the layout on the main thread by keeping enableWorker off.

content:
Common options#

These options apply to all layouts and define the reference size, center, worker
usage, and field mappings.

OPTION           DESCRIPTION                                                    TYPE                                                    DEFAULT
width / height   Reference size. Many layouts derive default centers/scales.    number                                                  undefined
center           Layout center. 2D uses [x, y], 3D uses [x, y, z].              [number, number] | [number, number, number]             undefined (layout-dependent)
enableWorker     Run in a Web Worker when available; fallback to main thread.   boolean                                                 false/undefined (layout-dependent)
node             Node field mapping for business data.                          (datum) => ({ id?, x?, y?, z?, parentId?, isCombo? })   undefined
edge             Edge field mapping for business data.                          (datum) => ({ id?, source?, target? })                  undefined

Node mapping fields#

 * id: unique node id, required.
 * x/y/z: optional initial coordinates for warm start or continuous layouts.
 * parentId: parent combo id for composite or nested layouts.
 * isCombo: whether this is a combo node.

Edge mapping fields#

 * source / target: endpoint node ids, required. Must match some node id.
 * id: optional edge id. Auto-generated if omitted.

3D extensions#

D3Force3DLayout adds z-axis forces on top of 2D. Node results include z and may
keep intermediate velocities like vz.

OPTION          DESCRIPTION                    TYPE                                         DEFAULT
numDimensions   Dimensions, fixed at 3.        3                                            3
center          Center force with z support.   false | { x?, y?, z?, strength? }            -
radial          Radial force with z support.   false | { radius?, x?, y?, z?, strength? }   -
z               Z-axis force                   false | { z?, strength? }                    -

Options#

This page lists all options for D3ForceLayout. It supports two configuration
styles:

 1. Shorthand fields: quick access to common settings like centerX,
    linkDistance, nodeStrength.
 2. Force objects: closer to the original d3-force API, such as link, manyBody,
    collide, x, y, center, radial.

You can mix both; when both are provided, the force objects are usually more
predictable.


Common options#

OPTION           DESCRIPTION                      TYPE                                                    DEFAULT
width / height   Reference size                   number                                                  undefined
enableWorker     Whether to run in a Web Worker   boolean                                                 false/undefined
node             Node field mapping               (datum) => ({ id?, x?, y?, z?, parentId?, isCombo? })   undefined
edge             Edge field mapping               (datum) => ({ id?, source?, target? })                  undefined

Note: D3ForceLayout does not use center; it uses centerX/centerY instead.


Shorthand fields#

OPTION                      DESCRIPTION                                           TYPE                             DEFAULT
onTick                      Tick callback                                         (layout) => void                 undefined
centerX / centerY           Center coordinates                                    number                           width/2, height/2
centerStrength              Center force strength in [0, 1]                       number                           undefined
edgeId                      Edge id accessor                                      (edge) => string                 (edge) => String(edge.id)
linkDistance                Ideal link length                                     number | (edge)=>number          50
edgeStrength                Link strength in [0, 1]                               number | (edge)=>number | null   null
edgeIterations              Link force iterations                                 number                           1
nodeStrength                Many-body strength; negative = repulsion              number | (node)=>number          -30
theta                       Barnes–Hut parameter in (0, 1]                        number                           undefined
distanceMax / distanceMin   Many-body distance range                              number                           undefined
preventOverlap              Prevent overlaps                                      boolean                          false
collideStrength             Collision strength in [0, 1]                          number                           1
collideIterations           Collision iterations                                  number                           1
nodeSize                    Node diameter used for collision radius               number | (node)=>number          10
nodeSpacing                 Extra spacing between nodes                           number | (node)=>number          0
radialRadius                Ideal radial radius                                   number                           100
radialStrength              Radial force strength in [0, 1]                       number                           undefined
radialX / radialY           Radial force center                                   number                           undefined
clustering                  Enable clustering                                     boolean                          false
clusterBy                   Cluster field/function                                (node)=>string|number            (d)=>d.cluster
clusterNodeStrength         In-cluster node strength                              number                           -1
clusterEdgeStrength         Inter-cluster edge strength                           number                           0.1
clusterEdgeDistance         Inter-cluster edge distance                           number                           100
clusterNodeSize             Cluster node size                                     number                           10
clusterFociStrength         Cluster focus strength in [0, 1]                      number                           0.8
iterations                  Force iterations; not the same as layout iterations   number                           undefined
forceSimulation             Custom d3 Simulation                                  Simulation                       undefined
alpha / alphaMin            Current/stop thresholds                               number                           undefined
alphaDecay                  Decay rate of alpha                                   number                           undefined
alphaTarget                 Target alpha                                          number                           undefined
velocityDecay               Velocity decay factor                                 number                           undefined
randomSource                Random generator                                      () => number                     undefined


Force objects#

These force objects can be set to false to disable; otherwise configure fields
as in d3-force.

collide#

 * radius?: number | (node, index, nodes) => number
 * strength?: number
 * iterations?: number

manyBody#

 * strength?: number | (node, index, nodes) => number
 * theta?: number
 * distanceMin?: number
 * distanceMax?: number

link#

 * id?: (edge, index, edges) => string
 * distance?: number | (edge, index, edges) => number
 * strength?: number | (edge, index, edges) => number
 * iterations?: number

x / y#

 * strength?: number | (node, index, nodes) => number
 * x?: number | (node, index, nodes) => number (only for x force)
 * y?: number | (node, index, nodes) => number (only for y force)


2D extensions#

OPTION   DESCRIPTION    TYPE
center   Center force   false | { x?, y?, strength? }
radial   Radial force   false | { radius?, x?, y?, strength? }

Iteration control#

These options control convergence for ForceLayout, ForceAtlas2Layout, and
FruchtermanLayout.

Execution modes#

 * execute(data): run in one go; frame-splitting is controlled by animate.
 * You can also wire layouts into your render loop via restart(), tick(n),
   stop(). See "Iterative layouts" in Common API.


Iteration options#

OPTION                  DESCRIPTION                                                    TYPE                     DEFAULT
maxIteration            Maximum iterations                                             number                   0/500 (layout-dependent)
minMovement             Convergence threshold. Stops when step size falls below this   number                   0/0.4 (layout-dependent)
                        value.
animate                 Run iterations in frames for visualization and interaction.    boolean                  true
dimensions              Dimensions: 2D or 3D.                                          2 | 3                    2
distanceThresholdMode   How to evaluate minMovement: mean, max, or min.                'mean' | 'max' | 'min'   'mean'
maxDistance             Maximum interaction distance; used by some algorithms.         number                   undefined
onTick                  Callback after each iteration; receives the layout instance.   (layout) => void         undefined
